increments.title: Content-bearing telemetry is captured by default and served over the API
increments.goal: Turn the content flags on by default in `argus env` and make the collector store and serve what the resulting events carry, so a caller can ask for the conversation content belonging to a point in time.
criteria: `argus env` includes the content flags by default in both output formats: user prompts, tool details, tool content, and the flag or flags the CLI requires to emit `api_request_body`/`api_response_body` events.
The exact flag names are verified against the CLI's monitoring documentation rather than assumed.
If the current CLI turns out not to emit request/response body events at all, that is reported as an explicit finding, naming the best content the available flags do provide.
What attribution actually arrives for subagent activity and for request bodies is established and reported, including any gap, so later increments know which records can be assigned to which agent.

The collector stores the content those events carry and exposes those content-bearing records over the JSON API like the existing signals, such that the content belonging to a point in time can be asked for.
Recordings made without the content flags are out of contract: no fallback rendering, no compatibility notice, and no test pins behavior for them.
`./test.sh` is green.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings: the four content flags (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT, OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1) are on by default in all four env formats, contentOf plus store.queryContent plus GET /api/content store and serve the content-bearing records with an inclusive 'at' bound, and the suite is green (156 argus cases exit 0; bash ./test.sh PASS all 6 suites). The attribution gap is established: body events carry query_source and span context but no agent.name or agent_id.

increments.title: A session opens on the timeline, with a lane per agent
increments.goal: Make opening a session in the argus UI land on a timeline view that draws one lane for the main session and one per subagent across each agent's lifetime, with the existing technical views reachable from it but subordinate.
criteria: Opening a session in the argus UI lands on the timeline view.
The previous technical views — event tail, traces, raw inspectors — remain reachable from the timeline view and are subordinate to it, not the other way round.

The timeline draws one lane for the main session and one lane per subagent instance, so two concurrent subagents of the same type get two lanes; `query_source` names only the agent type, and per-instance identity has to come from the span attributes the previous increment reported (`agent_id`, `parent_agent_id`).
Each agent lane spans that agent's lifetime, so any vertical slice answers which agents are running at that moment.

Where the run places the record-to-agent join — collector side or UI side — that choice is stated, and activity that cannot be attributed to an agent instance is shown as unattributed rather than dropped or silently folded into the main session.
increments.note: Criteria sharpened by what content-pipeline established: bodies carry no agent.name or agent_id, so lanes per agent instance can only come from the span join, and query_source alone cannot separate two subagents of one type. The researcher of this increment settles first where that join lives and what session data with the content flags on it can be built and exercised against, since scripts/demo-emit.mjs emits no content-bearing events.

return.plan:
GOAL. Opening a session in argus-ui lands on a timeline that draws one lane for the main session and one lane per subagent *instance*, each lane spanning that agent's lifetime. The old technical views stay, below the timeline, closed by default.

FACTS ESTABLISHED (verified against the installed Claude Code 2.1.224 binary at /opt/claude-code/bin/claude and against the code):
1. Only two span names carry agent identity: `claude_code.llm_request` and `claude_code.tool` set `agent_id` and `parent_agent_id`, and only when the agent context is NOT the main agent (`B6(e){return e.agentType==="main"}` guards it). So a span without `agent_id` is either main-agent work or a span type that never carries it.
2. `claude_code.interaction`, `claude_code.tool.execution`, `claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user` and `claude_code.hook` set NO agent attributes at all; they inherit the agent only through the span parent chain (they are started with the active span as parent).
3. There IS a `claude_code.subagent.spawn` span in the binary carrying `agent_id`/`agent_type`/`parent_agent_id`, but it is dead code in this build: its emitter starts with `if(!Xwe())return` and `function Xwe(){return!1}`. Do not build lane lifetimes on it and do not reference it.
4. `query_source` (e.g. `agent:builtin:researcher`) is set on `llm_request` spans and names only the agent type. `agent.name` is set by the attribution helper where the CLI knows the agent's name. Neither separates two concurrent instances of one type; `agent_id` does.
5. `parent_agent_id` of a top-level subagent is the main agent's id, and the main agent's id never appears as an `agent_id` on any span. So a `parent_agent_id` that matches no lane means "child of main".
6. The store already buffers every span (`store.spans`, bounded at 50 000, 24 h retention) with `sessionId`, `spanId`, `parentSpanId`, `traceId`, `name`, `startMs`, `endMs`, `durationMs`, `attrs`, `status`. There is no per-session span index; `queryEvents`/`queryContent` already do a full linear walk per request, so a walk is the house style.

DECISION — WHERE THE JOIN LIVES: collector side. The store already holds every span of the session indexed by nothing but a linear array, so the join is one pass over a bounded buffer, whereas UI-side would mean one `/api/traces/:id` fetch per trace in the browser. The claude-specific knowledge "which attribute names an agent" belongs with the rest of it in `tools/argus/src/claude.mjs`, and `tools/argus-ui` is forbidden from importing anything of argus, so a UI-side join would duplicate that knowledge in the browser. The later increments (lane activity, context at a time) need one vocabulary of instance ids to filter by; serving it once fixes it. Rejected: a UI-side join (N fetches, duplicated domain knowledge); a new persisted index in the store (eviction would have to be kept in step for no gain over the scan).

COLLECTOR CHANGES

A. `tools/argus/src/claude.mjs` — add one exported helper, next to `attributionOf`:
```js
/** The agent instance a record belongs to, or null when it carries no agent identity. */
export function agentRefOf(attrs = {}) {
  const agentId = typeof attrs.agent_id === 'string' ? attrs.agent_id.trim() : '';
  if (!agentId) return null;
  const parentAgentId = typeof attrs.parent_agent_id === 'string' ? attrs.parent_agent_id.trim() : '';
  const agentType = attrs['agent.name'] ?? attrs.query_source ?? null;
  return { agentId, parentAgentId: parentAgentId || null, agentType: agentType || null };
}
```
Document in its comment that the main agent emits no `agent_id`, so `null` means "not a subagent instance", not "unknown".

B. `tools/argus/src/store.mjs` — add `getAgents(sessionId)` in the queries section, after `getTrace`. Returns `null` for an unknown session (same contract as `getSession`), otherwise:
```js
{ sessionId, firstMs, lastMs, items: [lane, ...] }
```
with `lane = { id, kind, agentId, parentAgentId, agentType, firstMs, lastMs, durationMs, spanCount }`.
- `id` is `'main'`, `'unattributed'`, or `` `agent:${agentId}` `` — the prefix removes any collision between a real agent id and the two synthetic lanes.
- `kind` is `'main' | 'subagent' | 'unattributed'`.
Algorithm: take `this.spans.filter(s => s.sessionId === sessionId)`, build `byId = Map(spanId -> span)` over ALL of them (across traces, since a subagent's spans may sit in another trace than its parent's), then resolve each span to a lane key with memoisation and a depth cap of 64:
- `agentRefOf(span.attrs)` non-null -> `agent:<agentId>`;
- else no `parentSpanId` -> `main`;
- else parent present in `byId` -> the parent's lane key (recurse);
- else (parent missing from the buffer, or the depth cap hit) -> `unattributed`.
A missing parent is the one honest "cannot be attributed" case — the buffer evicts oldest first and `getTrace` already counts such orphans — and it must land on `unattributed`, never on `main`. Accumulate per lane: `firstMs = min(startMs)` over spans with `startMs > 0`, `lastMs = max(endMs || startMs)`, `durationMs = max(0, lastMs - firstMs)`, `spanCount`, and for subagent lanes fill `agentType`/`parentAgentId` from the first span that carries a non-null one. Order the items: the main lane first, then subagent lanes by `firstMs` and then `agentId`, then `unattributed` last. Top-level `firstMs`/`lastMs` are the min/max over the lanes, `0` when the session has no spans. A session with no spans yields `items: []` — lanes are built from spans and nothing is invented.

C. `tools/argus/src/server.mjs` — add, in `handleApi` next to the existing `^\/api\/sessions\/([^/]+)$` match, a route `^\/api\/sessions\/([^/]+)\/agents$`: `store.getAgents(id)`, `404 {error:'unknown session'}` when null, else `200` with the payload as-is. A path segment rather than `/api/agents?session=` so the unknown-session answer is the same 404 the sibling route already gives, with no new error shape to invent.

D. `tools/argus/scripts/demo-emit.mjs` — emit subagent work, so the timeline can be seen without a live agent run. In `buildTurn`, after the first LLM call, add a `claude_code.tool` span with `tool_name: 'Task'` on the main lane and, overlapping in time under it, two subagent instances with the SAME `query_source: 'agent:builtin:researcher'` and DIFFERENT `agent_id` (`agt_<hex>`), each also carrying `parent_agent_id: 'agt_main'`, each with one `claude_code.llm_request` span and one `claude_code.tool` span, plus one `claude_code.tool.execution` child under a subagent tool span that carries no agent attributes (it exercises parent-chain inheritance in the demo the way the CLI produces it). Do not fake orphans; the unattributed lane is not demo material.

E. `tools/argus/README.md` — one row in the HTTP API table: `GET /api/sessions/:id/agents` — "Agent lanes of a session: main, one per subagent instance, unattributed". Leave `skills/argus/SKILL.md` alone: its route table is a deliberate subset for reading numbers, not an API index.

UI CHANGES (tools/argus-ui, no change to `src/server.mjs` — `/api/` is already proxied wholesale, and `.js` is already in its MIME map)

F. New `public/format.js`: move `esc`, `fmtNum`, `fmtCost`, `fmtDur`, `fmtClock`, `fmtAgo`, `shortId` out of `public/app.js` verbatim and export them. A pure move, no behaviour change; it exists so the timeline module and `app.js` share one `esc` rather than two. Files in `public/` are `.js`, not `.mjs`, matching `app.js` and the server's MIME map.

G. New `public/timeline.js`, the testable half of the view. Exports:
- `SUBORDINATE_VIEWS` — the previous technical views, in order: `overview/Overview`, `todos/Tasks`, `traces/Traces`, `events/Events`, `metrics/Metrics`, `raw/Attributes` (the current `TABS` list, moved here).
- `DEFAULT_VIEW = null` — no technical view open, so a freshly opened session is the timeline alone.
- `agentLabel(lane)` — `'main session'` for main, `'unattributed'` for unattributed, otherwise the last `:`-separated segment of `agentType` (`agent:builtin:researcher` -> `researcher`), or `'subagent'` when `agentType` is null.
- `laneRows(items, { startMs, endMs })` — pure geometry: returns each lane with `depth`, `leftPct`, `widthPct` as numbers. `total = Math.max(endMs - startMs, 1)` so a zero-width window cannot divide by zero; `leftPct`/`widthPct` are clamped into `0..100`; a zero-duration lane keeps a `0.4` minimum width, as the waterfall does. `depth`: main and unattributed `0`; a subagent whose `parentAgentId` matches another lane's `agentId` is `1 + depth(parent)`, otherwise `1` (its parent is the main agent, whose id is never emitted as an `agent_id`); cap the walk so a cycle cannot hang it.
- `timelineHtml(items, window)` — the panel: an axis with 0/25/50/75/100 % ticks labelled `fmtClock`, one row per lane with an indented label (`agentLabel` plus, for subagents, the short `agentId`, so two instances of one type are told apart on screen), a bar positioned from the geometry, and the lane's duration. Bars carry `data-kind` = the lane kind. With no lanes it returns a placeholder in the wording of the existing traces placeholder: the timeline is drawn from spans, which need `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1` and `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp`. Everything interpolated goes through `esc`.
- `viewStripHtml(openId, counts)` — the subordinate strip, reusing the existing `.tabs`/`.tab` classes and `data-view` (not `data-tab`) buttons, `aria-selected` true only on the open one, count badges as today.

H. `public/app.js`: import from the two new modules and delete what moved. `state.tab` becomes `state.view`, initialised to `DEFAULT_VIEW`; add `state.agents = []` and `state.agentWindow = { startMs: 0, endMs: 0 }`. `loadSession()` also fetches `/api/sessions/<id>/agents` and stores `items` plus a window of `{ startMs: min(session.firstSeenMs, payload.firstMs || Infinity), endMs: max(session.lastSeenMs, payload.lastMs) }`, falling back to empty on error. `renderDetail()` renders: head, then `timelineHtml(...)` ALWAYS, then `viewStripHtml(state.view, counts)`, then `<div id="view-body">`; `renderViewBody()` (the renamed `renderTabBody`) renders nothing when `state.view` is null. Click wiring: `[data-view]` sets `state.view`, and clicking the open one closes it back to the timeline alone. `loadTabData` becomes `loadViewData` and returns early when no view is open. `selectSession()` resets `state.view = DEFAULT_VIEW`, which is what makes opening a session land on the timeline. The 15 s repaint's `state.tab === 'overview'` becomes `state.view === 'overview'`.

I. `public/styles.css` — a `.timeline` block after the waterfall block, reusing the same `--label-w` grid, `.axis-ticks`/`.axis-tick`: `.lane-row`, `.lane-label`, `.lane-track`, `.lane-bar` with `data-kind="main"` (`--violet`), `"subagent"` (`--accent`), `"unattributed"` (`--text-faint`), and an indent driven by an inline `padding-left` like `.span-label` uses. No new CSS variables.

J. `tools/argus-ui/README.md` — under "What it shows", a first bullet: **Timeline** — one lane for the main session and one per subagent instance over its lifetime; the other views listed after it as what opens below it. Do not extend the skeleton file list in `test/independence.test.mjs`: it names the project's structural minimum, not every file.

OUT OF THIS INCREMENT, by the brief: activity marks and the context-size curve on a lane, scrubbing and live mode, and the per-lane context/tool detail. Do not add a chosen-time marker, a per-lane activity block or a selection handler now.

return.testPlan:
WHETHER: tests are needed. Four of the five criteria have something a tool can check; the fifth (the join's placement) is a stated decision plus the unattributed rule, and the rule is testable.

I ran nothing — not the suites, not a baseline. Both suites are green as of the last increment's review (156 argus cases, exit 0) and nothing is known red; the first run belongs to whoever runs it downstream. The only thing I executed was `grep` over the installed CLI binary to settle which spans carry `agent_id`, which is a reading, not a test run.

WHAT AND HOW, per criterion.

--- Criterion: the timeline draws one lane for the main session and one lane per subagent instance; two concurrent subagents of the same type get two lanes; identity comes from agent_id/parent_agent_id.

Level: unit, against the store. File: `tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs`. Framework: `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`. Conventions of that file: no server, a bare `new TelemetryStore()` per case, fixtures from the local `span(name, attributes, extra)` / `log(...)` / `metric(...)` builders at the top of the file — `span` already takes `{ spanId, parentSpanId, startMs, endMs }` as offsets from a module-level `NOW` (absolute past timestamps get evicted by retention, so keep using it), sets `traceId: 'trace-1'` and `attrs['session.id'] = SESSION`; records go in via `store.ingest('traces', [...])`; test names are lowercase sentences stating the fact. Add a small local helper for a subagent span (`agent_id`, `parent_agent_id`, `query_source`) rather than repeating the attribute literals. Command: `node --test tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs`.

1. Main only. Ingest an interaction span (no parent, no agent_id) and an llm_request child of it, no agent attributes. `store.getAgents(SESSION)` returns exactly one item, `kind === 'main'`, `id === 'main'`, `spanCount === 2`.
2. Two instances of one type — the headline case. Ingest a main interaction span plus, under it, two `claude_code.tool` spans with `agent_id: 'agt-a'` and `agent_id: 'agt-b'`, BOTH with `query_source: 'agent:builtin:researcher'` and `parent_agent_id: 'agt-main'`, with overlapping but different start/end offsets. Expect three items: one `main`, two `subagent` with ids `agent:agt-a` and `agent:agt-b`, each carrying `agentType === 'agent:builtin:researcher'` and `parentAgentId === 'agt-main'`. The two lanes must not be merged.
3. Instance identity beats type. Same as case 2 but assert the item ids are distinct and `items.filter(i => i.kind === 'subagent').length === 2` — pins that `query_source` alone never collapses two instances.
4. Ordering. In case 2's fixture, assert `items[0].kind === 'main'` and that the two subagent lanes come in ascending `firstMs`.
5. Session isolation. Ingest a subagent span for a second session id and assert it does not appear in the first session's items.
6. Unknown session. `store.getAgents('nope')` returns `null`.
7. A session with records but no spans (ingest one log only) returns `{ items: [] }` with `firstMs === 0`.

--- Criterion: each agent lane spans that agent's lifetime.

Level: unit, same file, same conventions, same command.

8. Lifetime from the extremes. A subagent with three spans at offsets (start 100/end 400), (start 200/end 900), (start 300/end 500): the lane has `firstMs === NOW+100`, `lastMs === NOW+900`, `durationMs === 800`.
9. Open span edge. A span with `endMs: 0` contributes its `startMs` to `lastMs` and does not push the lane to the epoch or to NaN.
10. A span with `startMs: 0` (never started / not decoded) does not drag `firstMs` to 0.

--- Criterion: activity that cannot be attributed to an agent instance is shown as unattributed, not dropped and not folded into the main session.

Level: unit, same file, same conventions, same command.

11. Inheritance through the parent chain. A `claude_code.tool.execution` span with NO agent attributes whose `parentSpanId` is a subagent's tool span lands on that subagent's lane, not on main. (This is the real CLI shape: only llm_request and tool spans carry agent_id.)
12. Broken chain. A span with no agent attributes whose `parentSpanId` names a span that is not in the buffer produces an `unattributed` lane holding it — assert the lane exists with `kind === 'unattributed'`, that its `spanCount` is 1, and that the main lane's `spanCount` did not absorb it.
13. Unattributed is last. With main, one subagent and one orphan present, `items.at(-1).kind === 'unattributed'`.
14. No orphans, no lane. With every parent resolvable, no item has `kind === 'unattributed'`.

--- The agent-identity helper.

Level: unit. File: `tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs`. Framework and conventions: `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, plain calls with literal attribute objects, one `test('…')` per fact, names as lowercase sentences. Command: `node --test tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs`.

15. `agentRefOf({ agent_id: 'agt-a', parent_agent_id: 'agt-main', query_source: 'agent:builtin:researcher' })` returns `{ agentId: 'agt-a', parentAgentId: 'agt-main', agentType: 'agent:builtin:researcher' }`.
16. `agentRefOf({ query_source: 'main' })` returns `null` — a main-agent span carries no agent_id and must not become an instance.
17. `agentRefOf({ agent_id: '' })` and `agentRefOf({})` return `null`.
18. `agent.name` wins over `query_source` as the type when both are present.

--- The route that serves the lanes.

Level: integration over HTTP. File: `tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs`. Framework: `node:test` + `node:assert/strict` with the file's existing `withServer({}, async ({ base }) => …)` helper (real `TelemetryStore` + `createServer`, bound to port 0) and its OTLP payload builders — follow `tracePayload(sessionId)` for protobuf spans or the JSON logs builders for the JSON shape; build the span payload with the same `encodeMessage(..., EXPORT_TRACE_REQUEST)` route and `T0` nanosecond timestamps that `tracePayload` uses, and assert the ingest POST returned 200 before asserting on the query, as the content case does. Command: `node --test tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs`.

19. POST a trace payload for one session holding an interaction span plus two subagent tool spans of one `query_source` with distinct `agent_id`; `GET /api/sessions/<id>/agents` answers 200 with `items.length === 3`, kinds `['main','subagent','subagent']`, and each item carrying numeric `firstMs`, `lastMs`, `durationMs` and `spanCount`.
20. `GET /api/sessions/nope/agents` answers 404 with `{ error: 'unknown session' }`.

--- Criterion: opening a session lands on the timeline, and the previous technical views stay reachable and subordinate.

Level: unit over the view module. File: `tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs` — NEW. Framework: `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, importing `../public/timeline.js` directly; the module must not touch `document`, `window` or `location` at import time, and none of these cases may use a DOM. Conventions to follow, taken from the two existing argus-ui test files: a top-of-file comment saying what the file pins, one `test('…')` per fact with a lowercase-sentence name, `assert.equal`/`assert.deepEqual`/`assert.match`, no shared mutable state between cases, and small local fixture builders instead of a framework. A lane fixture builder — `lane({ id, kind, agentId, parentAgentId, agentType, firstMs, lastMs })` — belongs at the top. Command: `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs`.

21. `DEFAULT_VIEW` is `null`, so nothing but the timeline is open when a session is opened.
22. `SUBORDINATE_VIEWS` still offers every previous technical view: its ids are exactly `['overview','todos','traces','events','metrics','raw']`, in that order.
23. `viewStripHtml(null, {})` marks no view as selected — no `aria-selected="true"` in the markup — and still contains a button for each of the six ids.
24. `viewStripHtml('events', {})` marks exactly one, and it is the events one.

--- Criterion: the lanes are drawn, one per agent, over each lifetime (the view half).

Same file, same conventions, same command.

25. Geometry. A lane covering the middle half of the window gets `leftPct === 25` and `widthPct === 50`.
26. Clamping. A lane starting before the window and ending after it gets `leftPct === 0` and `widthPct === 100`.
27. Zero-width window (`startMs === endMs`) yields finite numbers for every lane — assert `Number.isFinite` on both, and no `NaN` in the rendered markup.
28. A zero-duration lane keeps the `0.4` minimum width, so an instant agent is still visible.
29. Depth. Main is depth 0; a subagent whose `parentAgentId` matches no lane is depth 1; a subagent whose `parentAgentId` matches another subagent lane's `agentId` is depth 2; the unattributed lane is depth 0.
30. `agentLabel`: `agent:builtin:researcher` renders as `researcher`; a null `agentType` renders as `subagent`; the main lane as `main session`; the unattributed lane as `unattributed`.
31. Two instances of one type are distinguishable on screen: `timelineHtml` for two lanes with the same `agentType` and different `agentId` contains both agent ids (assert each with `assert.match`) and produces two lane rows.
32. Empty state: `timelineHtml([], window)` returns a placeholder whose text mentions spans (assert with a `/span/i` match), not an empty panel.
33. Escaping: a lane whose `agentType` is `<script>x</script>` appears escaped — assert the markup contains no literal `<script`.

DELIBERATELY UNTESTED, and why:
- The browser rendering itself, and that a click on a subordinate view opens it below the timeline. There is no DOM harness in this project and adding one means a runtime dependency, which `tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md` forbids without asking the human. What is pinned instead is the view model — `DEFAULT_VIEW`, `SUBORDINATE_VIEWS`, the strip markup — plus the fact that `app.js` renders the timeline unconditionally, which a reader can check.
- `public/styles.css`: no test asserts appearance.

return.summary: Closed content-pipeline as done (review accepted, no findings) and re-cut the four open increments against what it showed. Three changes, each traceable to a finding of that increment. (1) tools-at-time is dropped and its three criteria moved into context-at-time: the increment established that tool parameters and request bodies are the same class of content record, served by the same endpoint under the same session/kind/time bound and needing the same per-agent join, so the selected-lane detail panel is one change rather than two full chains. (2) timeline-landing's lane criterion is sharpened: body events carry query_source and span context but no agent.name and no agent_id, and query_source names only the agent type, so two concurrent subagents of one type are indistinguishable without joining through the span attributes agent_id/parent_agent_id; the increment now also has to state where that join lives and to show unattributable activity as unattributed rather than folding it into the main session. (3) lane-activity gains one criterion: bodies are truncated at the CLI's content ceiling while the untruncated length is reported separately, so the context-size curve must come from a recorded size and the view must name which measure it draws. scrub-live is unchanged. Criterion coverage of the issue: env flags and collector storage/serving, the flag-name verification, the attribution finding, the out-of-contract rule for flagless recordings and ./test.sh green sit in content-pipeline (done); landing on the timeline with the technical views subordinate, and lanes per agent over their lifetime, in timeline-landing; activity plus the context-size curve in lane-activity; scrubbing and live mode in scrub-live; the structured context message list and the per-agent tool listing in context-at-time. Two facts the cut turns on that I could not settle and deliberately left to the next researcher rather than to a question: whether the record-to-agent join belongs in the collector or in the UI (the UI already proxies every /api/ path, so either is open), and what session data the UI increments can be built against, since scripts/demo-emit.mjs emits no content-bearing events and no recording with the flags on is known to exist. I rejected splitting an agent-resolution API off as its own increment: it would deliver nothing a reader can judge on its own and may be unnecessary if the join is done UI-side. One operational fact for later steps: test.sh is committed mode 100644, so `./test.sh` exits 126 on this checkout and the suite has to be run as `bash ./test.sh` (exit 0, PASS all 6 suites) — a pre-existing checkout fact, not a defect of the change. Backlog now holds 6 increments (1 done, 1 dropped, 4 todo), so at most 5 of the 8 chains are spent if every remaining one takes a single pass.
